_what: Word triggers that tie a job description to one of George's assets or receipts. scripts/asset_hits.py scans every gathered description with these and prints the hits per job, so the match is mechanical, not memory. Each entry: words = regexes (case-insensitive); say = the one line a letter or answer uses; proof = where it can be checked; status = where it lives as of the date. Refresh status with scripts/check_assets.py. Built 2026-10-27 from me/assets.md and me/george-dossier.md. 2026-10-27: 'weight' and 'card' per entry (George's rule: FULL = in use or in the pipeline; LESS = GitHub-only or a paper, backs a letter but never leads).

WiM.say: I built WiM, a voice-to-text Android app with a speech-disfluency layer, in Google Play testing with pricing live; sole inventor on its 35-claim US provisional patent (App. No. 64/100,336).
WiM.status: Play closed testing (vc658, 10/13/2026); testers next, then production

Patent.say: Sole inventor on US provisional patent App. No. 64/100,336 (filed June 27 2026, 35 claims): an assistive overlay that reconstructs disfluent speech and clarifies uncertain words without disturbing the host app; I wrote the application myself.

NoiseFile.say: I built and shipped NoiseFile, a Google Play app that checks a noise complaint against the city's own ordinance across 36 Bay Area cities and files it the way that city wants.
NoiseFile.proof: github.com/gugosf114/noisefile-android (public); Google Play listing 'Neighbor Noise Complaint Kit'
NoiseFile.status: LIVE on Google Play (production, update 10/27/2026; first sale)
